subject.title: Proposal: Integration des Iroh Frameworks für direkte P2P Gateway-Verbindungen (iOS/App)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class Iroh-based peer-to-peer transport for Gateway clients, or retain the current SSH/Tailscale/LAN/WebSocket remote-access model?
rationale: This chooses a new transport, dependency/runtime boundary, mobile setup workflow, credential model, and operator support commitment; source inspection cannot determine whether that product and security direction is desired.

options.title: Keep current transport model
options.body: Close or move this proposal out of product docs and continue documenting the supported SSH, Tailscale, LAN/Tailnet, and direct WebSocket paths.

options.title: Sponsor a design phase
options.body: Convert the idea into a scoped design issue that defines protocol integration, authentication and pairing, ticket lifecycle, relay trust, mobile lifecycle, upgrade behavior, and proof requirements before implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep current transport model
recommendation.body: Close or move this proposal out of product docs and continue documenting the supported SSH, Tailscale, LAN/Tailnet, and direct WebSocket paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the documented remote Gateway access model makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the transport-direction decision.
